facts.value: first community at Meaux 1546, first national synod at Paris 1559

citations.excerpt: The first Protestant community in France was that of Meaux (1546) organized on the lines of the church at Strassburg of which Calvin was pastor.
The church at Paris was commissioned to summon the first synod, which in spite of the danger of persecution met on the 25th of May 1559.

facts.value: French Protestants, organized on Calvin's model. They obtained the Edict of Nantes in 1598, which was revoked on 18 October 1685.

citations.excerpt: French Protestantism received from Calvin its first organization and the form which has since become traditional
obtained by their constancy the promulgation of the Edict of Nantes (April 13, 1598), the charter of religion and political freedom
on the 18th of October 1685 he pronounced its revocation.

facts.value_before_verify: French Reformed Protestants, organized on Calvin's model. They gained toleration by the Edict of Nantes in 1598, which Louis XIV revoked in 1685.
